questions.subject: English
questions.prompt:
Read the passage and answer the question.

As a veteran pedagogue of language and communication with experience spanning over three decades, I've never been unintrigued by the symbiotic relationship among the four language skills: listening, speaking, reading and writing. So intriguing is it that I always tend to go "overboard" when in a discourse regarding them.

This effort is nevertheless going to be limited in scope to the primal of the four which is one of the two not acquired by learning but by natural acquisition as a gift of providence to mankind. It is crucial to point out here that listening, by its natural configuration is the only one that can never come in excess as a virtue. Who then is a listener? It turns out that the one whose listening acumen is top-notch is the gainer and never the loser. Children who listen to parents end up succeeding and by extension, satisfy the desire of their Maker. A government that listens to the yearnings of the governed remains eternally popular even long after its tenure has ended.

In candour, good listeners never miss anything good because effective listening is an unmistakable tool for excellence. In my curiosity, I discovered that good listeners are winners as students, government workers, servants in God's vineyard and in all spheres of human endeavour they find themselves. The one who listens raptly is the best arbiter. How will one arbitrate in a controversy involving two or more parties and one is benefit of effective listening skills? This is almost impossible lest judgement becomes lopsided.

A good listener easily identifies problems and is able to proffer appropriate and timely solutions to the issues raised. It seems unarguable that effective listening is that which enhances knowledge acquisition in a way that is devoid of doubts and fear of contradictions. Equally worthy of note is that good listeners are trusted and easily build relationships with people around them. Suffice to round off by asserting that the effective listener is the true leader and the real leader indeed.

The style of the passage is
questions.explanation: The passage explains the value and benefits of effective listening, developing the subject through clarification and supporting points. Its dominant purpose is to inform and explain, which is expository writing.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. The writer explains a concept and its importance using supporting statements.
optionExplanations.B: Argumentative writing primarily attempts to persuade an audience to accept a contested position; persuasion is not the passage's dominant structure.
optionExplanations.C: Narrative writing recounts events in a sequence. The passage does not tell a sustained story.
optionExplanations.D: Descriptive writing focuses on detailed sensory portrayal of a person, place or thing; that is not the passage's main purpose.

optionExplanations.A: This is a feature of monopoly: barriers such as legal restrictions, patents or high start-up costs deter competitors.
optionExplanations.B: Correct. Many close substitutes weaken monopoly power and are not a defining feature of a pure monopoly.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. This is the statement that is NOT true; the Middle Belt does not have the country's highest population density.
optionExplanations.B: This is a commonly noted characteristic of the Middle Belt.
optionExplanations.C: Guinea Savanna is a major vegetation type in the region.
optionExplanations.D: The Middle Belt is commonly described as a transitional zone between northern and southern Nigeria.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.topic: Population and settlement — population density patterns
questions.prompt: On a population map of the world, all but one of the following generally appear as regions of low population density. Which is the exception?
questions.explanation: River valleys and deltas often support dense settlement because of fertile soils, water availability, transport routes and economic activity. Polar regions, hot deserts and equatorial rainforests generally have low population densities because of harsh climatic or environmental conditions.

optionExplanations.A: Polar and sub-polar regions generally have sparse populations.
optionExplanations.B: Hot deserts generally have sparse populations because of water scarcity and harsh conditions.
optionExplanations.C: Correct. River valleys and deltas are often densely populated, so they are the exception.
optionExplanations.D: Equatorial rainforest regions are often sparsely populated because dense vegetation, humidity and disease environments can constrain settlement.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.prompt: A fog is most likely to develop when a

options.A: Warm, moist wind blows over a cold current
options.B: Cold, dry wind blows over a warm current
options.C: Warm, moist wind blows over a warm current
options.D: Warm, dry wind blows over a cold current

questions.explanation: When warm, moist air moves over a colder surface or current, it is cooled to its dew point. Water vapour then condenses into tiny droplets suspended near the ground, producing advection fog.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. Cooling warm, moist air over a cold current can bring it to saturation and form fog.
optionExplanations.B: Cold, dry air is not the moist air mass required for this fog formation process.
optionExplanations.C: A warm current does not normally cool the warm, moist air sufficiently to produce this type of fog.
optionExplanations.D: Dry air contains less water vapour and is less likely to produce fog under these conditions.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.prompt: A typical example of a landform produced by marine erosion is a
questions.explanation: A stack is an isolated pillar of rock left offshore after waves erode a headland through the development and collapse of caves and arches. Spits, beaches and mudflats are primarily depositional coastal features.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. A stack is formed by wave erosion of a headland.
optionExplanations.B: A spit is formed by deposition of sediment transported by longshore drift.
optionExplanations.C: A beach is an accumulation of deposited sediment.
optionExplanations.D: A mudflat is a depositional feature formed in sheltered coastal environments.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.prompt: Which of the following is an example of a fossil fuel?
questions.explanation: Coal is a combustible sedimentary rock formed from ancient plant material subjected to burial, heat and pressure over geological time. Clay, granite and sandstone are not fossil fuels.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. Coal is a fossil fuel formed from ancient organic matter.
optionExplanations.B: Clay is a sedimentary material, not a fuel.
optionExplanations.C: Granite is an igneous rock.
optionExplanations.D: Sandstone is a sedimentary rock, not a fossil fuel.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.prompt: Great Britain and Germany are trading partners of West African countries from which region?
questions.explanation: Great Britain and Germany are European countries. In the broad regional classification used in geography, both are in Western Europe.

optionExplanations.A: Great Britain and Germany are not in South America.
optionExplanations.B: The Far East refers to East and Southeast Asia, not these countries.
optionExplanations.C: Correct. Great Britain and Germany are in Western Europe.
optionExplanations.D: North America includes countries such as Canada, the United States and Mexico.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.prompt: How were the major mountain belts of the world produced?
questions.explanation: Many major mountain belts, including the Himalayas and Alps, formed through crustal compression and folding associated with plate convergence. Erosion and weathering modify mountains but are not the primary processes that formed these major folded belts.

optionExplanations.A: Wind erosion forms and modifies landforms but does not create the major folded mountain belts.
optionExplanations.B: Glacial erosion carves mountain landscapes but does not form the major folded belts.
optionExplanations.C: Correct. Compression at convergent plate boundaries can fold and uplift rock layers.
optionExplanations.D: Weathering breaks down rock in place and does not create major mountain belts.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.prompt: In which of the following countries is commercial grain farming an important occupation?
questions.explanation: Canada has extensive temperate grassland and prairie regions where large-scale mechanised commercial grain farming, particularly wheat production, is important.

optionExplanations.A: Spain has commercial agriculture, but it is not the intended major grain-farming example in this item.
optionExplanations.B: Correct. Canada's prairie provinces are major commercial grain-producing regions.
optionExplanations.C: Kenya is better known for other agricultural systems and crops in this context.
optionExplanations.D: Nigeria has grain production, but not the same extensive mechanised commercial grain-farming system represented by Canada's prairies.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.prompt: Industries are broadly classified into

options.C: Mining, furniture making and cocoa processing

questions.explanation: The broad economic classification divides activities into primary (extracting or harvesting resources), secondary (manufacturing and construction) and tertiary (services).

optionExplanations.A: Correct. These are the three broad sectors of economic activity.
optionExplanations.B: These are examples of specific activities, not the complete broad classification.
optionExplanations.C: These are individual industries, not the three broad sectors.
optionExplanations.D: Manufacturing is part of the secondary sector, not a separate third sector.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.prompt: Inter-regional trade between countries in West Africa is promoted mainly by

options.A: Competition among the nations in Africa
options.C: Deliberate government policies in recent times

questions.explanation: Policies that reduce trade barriers, improve transport links and support regional integration can promote trade among West African countries. Producing similar goods may limit complementarity, while historical colonial links do not explain the main policy-driven expansion.

optionExplanations.A: Competition alone does not create the institutional conditions needed for increased trade.
optionExplanations.B: Producing similar goods can reduce the scope for mutually beneficial exchange.
optionExplanations.C: Correct. Government policies and regional integration measures can promote inter-regional trade.
optionExplanations.D: Historical colonial ties are not the principal contemporary policy mechanism.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.prompt: Mixed farming implies

options.A: Growing crops and rearing animals on a given land area
options.B: Growing grains and root crops on the same piece of land
options.C: Keeping poultry and rearing pigs on one and the same farm
options.D: Mixed cultivation of wheat, barley and oats

questions.explanation: Mixed farming is an agricultural system in which crop production and livestock rearing are practised together on the same farm. It is broader than growing several crop types or keeping only different kinds of livestock.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. Mixed farming combines crop cultivation and animal husbandry on one farm.
optionExplanations.B: This describes mixed cropping rather than mixed farming.
optionExplanations.C: This describes livestock diversification, not the full crop-and-livestock system.
optionExplanations.D: This is the cultivation of several crops, not the defining mixed-farming combination.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.prompt: More hydroelectric power projects should be constructed in Tropical Africa mainly because

options.B: There is an absence of waterfalls on rivers
options.C: There is an increasing demand for power

questions.explanation: Growing populations, urbanisation and industrial activity increase electricity demand. Hydroelectric projects can help meet that demand where suitable river flow, relief and infrastructure are available.

optionExplanations.A: A shortage of skilled labour would be a constraint, not the main reason to construct more projects.
optionExplanations.B: The absence of waterfalls is not generally true and is not the stated demand-side reason.
optionExplanations.C: Correct. Rising demand for electricity is the principal reason identified.
optionExplanations.D: Scanty rainfall would generally constrain hydroelectric generation rather than justify expansion.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: In this question, choose the option NEAREST IN MEANING to the underlined word: The minister's explanation was full of platitudes.
questions.explanation: A platitude is a commonplace or overused remark that sounds meaningful but offers little original thought. “Empty remarks” is the closest option.

optionExplanations.C: Difficult terms are not necessarily platitudes.
optionExplanations.D: Official statements are defined by their source, not by being trite.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: In this question, choose the option NEAREST IN MEANING to the underlined word: The candidate was praised for his perspicacity.
questions.explanation: Perspicacity means keen mental perception or the ability to understand matters clearly and quickly. “Clever insight” is the closest meaning.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. Perspicacity is keen insight or perceptiveness.
optionExplanations.B: A loud voice concerns volume, not mental perception.
optionExplanations.C: Physical strength is unrelated to the word.
optionExplanations.D: Moral weakness is unrelated and does not convey perceptiveness.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: In this question, choose the option NEAREST IN MEANING to the underlined word: The principal objected to the proposal because it was inimical to discipline.
questions.explanation: Inimical means hostile or harmful to something. The proposal was opposed because it would have a damaging effect on discipline.

optionExplanations.A: Helpful is the opposite of inimical in this context.
optionExplanations.B: Correct. Inimical means harmful or hostile.
optionExplanations.C: Relevant means connected to the matter, not harmful.
optionExplanations.D: Similar means alike and is unrelated.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: In this question, choose the option NEAREST IN MEANING to the underlined word: The student's behaviour was reprehensible.
questions.explanation: Reprehensible describes conduct that is deserving of criticism or blame. “Blameworthy” expresses this meaning directly.

optionExplanations.A: Admirable means worthy of praise, the opposite of reprehensible.
optionExplanations.B: Correct. Reprehensible means deserving blame or strong disapproval.
optionExplanations.C: Childish means immature and is not the direct meaning.
optionExplanations.D: Funny means amusing and is unrelated.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: In this question, choose the option NEAREST IN MEANING to the underlined word: The witness gave a spurious account of the event.
questions.explanation: Spurious means false, fake or not genuine. A spurious account is therefore an untrue or fabricated account.

optionExplanations.A: An account can be detailed without being spurious.
optionExplanations.B: Correct. Spurious means false or not genuine.
optionExplanations.C: Accurate is the opposite of spurious.
optionExplanations.D: Emotional describes tone, not truthfulness.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: Choose the option OPPOSITE IN MEANING to the underlined word: Her response was audacious.
questions.explanation: Audacious means bold, daring or willing to take risks. “Timid” means shy or lacking courage, so it is the opposite.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. Timid is the opposite of bold or audacious.
optionExplanations.B: Bold is a synonym of audacious.
optionExplanations.C: Rude concerns manners and is not the direct antonym.
optionExplanations.D: Stubborn means obstinate, not the opposite of audacious.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: Choose the option OPPOSITE IN MEANING to the underlined word: The minister's statement was deliberately equivocal.
questions.explanation: Equivocal means ambiguous or open to more than one interpretation. A direct statement is clear and unambiguous, making “direct” the closest opposite.

optionExplanations.A: Ambiguous is a synonym of equivocal.
optionExplanations.B: Correct. Direct means clear and unambiguous.
optionExplanations.C: Brief concerns length, not clarity.
optionExplanations.D: Official concerns status or authority, not ambiguity.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: Choose the option OPPOSITE IN MEANING to the underlined word: The principal's decision was incontrovertible.
questions.explanation: Incontrovertible means impossible to dispute or deny. “Open to debate” expresses the opposite: something that can reasonably be questioned or contested.

optionExplanations.A: Undeniable is a synonym of incontrovertible.
optionExplanations.B: Indisputable is also a synonym.
optionExplanations.C: Irrevocable means unable to be changed; it does not mean disputable.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. Open to debate is the opposite of incontrovertible.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: Choose the option OPPOSITE IN MEANING to the underlined word: The old scholar had always lived a gregarious life, constantly hosting gatherings and engaging with his peers.
questions.explanation: Gregarious describes someone who enjoys company and social interaction. Reclusive describes someone who avoids company and prefers to remain apart from others.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. Reclusive is the opposite of sociable or gregarious.
optionExplanations.B: Affable means friendly and sociable.
optionExplanations.C: Jovial means cheerful and is not the opposite.
optionExplanations.D: Extroverted is close in meaning to gregarious.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: Choose the option that BEST COMPLETES the sentence: The workload this semester is .............. than I expected.
questions.explanation: The word “than” signals a comparative construction. “Heavier” is the comparative form of “heavy”, and “very much” can intensify it. “More heavier” incorrectly uses two comparative markers.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect. “Heavier” is already comparative; adding “more” is redundant.
optionExplanations.B: “Much too heavy” does not form the required comparative construction with “than”.
optionExplanations.C: “So much heavy” is not grammatical in this sentence.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. “Very much heavier than I expected” is grammatical.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: The teacher asked the students to .............. the meaning of the difficult words in the dictionary.
questions.explanation: To look up a word means to search for its meaning or information about it, typically in a dictionary or reference work.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. “Look up” means consult a reference source for information.
optionExplanations.B: “Look for” means search for something, but it does not specifically express consulting a dictionary for a definition.
optionExplanations.C: “Look after” means take care of someone or something.
optionExplanations.D: “Look into” means investigate or examine a matter.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: Choose the option that BEST COMPLETES the sentence: The situation became .............. after the announcement.
questions.explanation: “Worse” is already the irregular comparative form of “bad”. “Much” can intensify a comparative adjective, so “much worse” is the correct expression.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect. “Worse” is already comparative; “more” is redundant.
optionExplanations.B: Correct. “Much” appropriately intensifies the comparative “worse”.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect. “Most worse” combines forms incorrectly.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect. This uses redundant comparative marking.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: Choose the option that BEST COMPLETES the sentence: The glass broke into pieces because of the .............. force of the impact.
questions.explanation: “Sheer” can mean complete, utter or very great in degree. The phrase “sheer force” means the great force of the impact. “Shear” refers to cutting or a force acting parallel to a surface.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. “Sheer force” is the appropriate expression.
optionExplanations.B: “Shear” refers to cutting or a type of mechanical force, not the intended adjective here.
optionExplanations.C: “Share” means a portion or to divide something.
optionExplanations.D: “Cheer” means encouragement or a shout of approval.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: No sooner had Tobi left the house _____ it began to rain.
questions.explanation: The standard correlative construction is “no sooner … than”. The first event is immediately followed by the second: no sooner had Tobi left than it began to rain.

optionExplanations.A: “Since” does not complete the fixed construction “no sooner … than”.
optionExplanations.B: “That” is not used in this correlative structure.
optionExplanations.C: Correct. “No sooner” is paired with “than”.
optionExplanations.D: “When” is normally paired with “hardly” or “scarcely”, not “no sooner”.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: The _____ of armed robbery has been on the increase.
questions.explanation: Incidence refers to the rate or frequency with which something occurs. The sentence concerns an increasing frequency of armed robbery.

optionExplanations.D: Correct. Incidence means rate or frequency of occurrence.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: The teacher asked the students to submit their assignments before the end of ____ week.

optionExplanations.A: “Last week” refers to the past and does not fit a future deadline.
optionExplanations.B: “Any week” does not identify the intended upcoming deadline.
optionExplanations.C: “These week” is ungrammatical; the determiner would be “this”.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. “Before the end of next week” is the natural future expression.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: He presented a masterpiece at the conference, ___________?
questions.explanation: The statement is affirmative and uses the simple past verb “presented”. A negative question tag is formed with “didn't” and the subject pronoun “he”.

optionExplanations.A: “Was he” does not match the simple past lexical verb “presented”.
optionExplanations.B: “Wasn't he” uses the wrong auxiliary for this sentence.
optionExplanations.C: A positive tag is not normally used after this affirmative statement.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. The negative tag is “didn't he?”.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: The building was haunted by a couple of spooks. The word “spooks” means
questions.explanation: “Spook” is an informal noun meaning a ghost or apparition. In the context of a haunted building, “ghosts” is the appropriate synonym.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. A spook is an informal term for a ghost.
optionExplanations.B: Robbers are criminals and do not fit the meaning.
optionExplanations.C: Hyenas are animals and are unrelated to the sentence.
optionExplanations.D: Hunters are people who hunt animals and do not fit the context.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word “natives” in the sentence: The natives were allowed to stay.
questions.explanation: Natives are people belonging originally to a particular place. “Foreigners” are people from elsewhere and provide the clearest opposite among the options.

optionExplanations.A: Immigrants are people who move into a country; this is a narrower category than foreigners.
optionExplanations.B: Correct. Foreigners are people who are not native to the place.
optionExplanations.C: Indigenes is a synonym of natives.
optionExplanations.D: Visitors are temporary guests and do not express the broad antonym as directly.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: Choose the option opposite in meaning to “protagonist”: Andrew is the protagonist in the play.
questions.explanation: A protagonist is the principal character in a literary work. An antagonist is the character or force that opposes the protagonist, making it the conventional contrasting term.

optionExplanations.A: An enemy may oppose someone, but it is not the specific literary term.

optionExplanations.C: Progressive means favouring progress and is unrelated.
optionExplanations.D: Opponent is a general term, while antagonist is the precise literary term.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: Despite his wealth, Mr Oluboye is known for tightening his belt. This means that

options.C: He refuses to wear a belt at all.

questions.explanation: The idiom “tighten one's belt” means to reduce spending and live more economically. It is figurative, not a reference to wearing a physical belt.

optionExplanations.B: Correct. It means spending less and being economical.
optionExplanations.C: This is a literal interpretation and misses the idiom.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: Which of the following words rhymes with “home”?

optionExplanations.D: This incorrectly places stress on the final syllable.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.explanation: First, P ∪ Q = {2, 3, 4, 5, 6}. Its complement in U is {1}. Intersecting {1} with R = {1, 2, 3, 4} gives {1}.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.prompt: Divide 4x³ − 3x + 1 by 2x − 1.
questions.explanation: Divide the leading terms: 4x³ ÷ 2x = 2x². Subtracting (2x − 1)(2x²) leaves 2x² − 3x + 1. Next add x to the quotient; subtracting (2x − 1)x leaves −2x + 1. Finally add −1, which removes the remainder. The quotient is 2x² + x − 1.

optionExplanations.A: Multiplying this by 2x − 1 does not reproduce the dividend.
optionExplanations.B: This has the wrong sign on the linear term and does not divide the polynomial exactly.
optionExplanations.C: This leaves a non-zero remainder when multiplied by 2x − 1.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. (2x − 1)(2x² + x − 1) = 4x³ − 3x + 1.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.prompt: The sum of two numbers is twice their difference. If the difference of the numbers is p, find the larger of the two numbers.
questions.explanation: Let the larger number be x and the smaller be y. The difference gives x − y = p. The sum is twice the difference, so x + y = 2p. Adding the equations gives 2x = 3p, hence x = 3p/2.

optionExplanations.A: This is not obtained from the sum and difference equations.
optionExplanations.B: Correct. Adding x − y = p and x + y = 2p gives 2x = 3p.
optionExplanations.C: This exceeds the value obtained by solving the simultaneous equations.
optionExplanations.D: This is twice the larger number found from the equations.

questions.subject: Geography

optionExplanations.D: Partial darkness is not the defining effect of the equinox.

questions.subject: Geography

questions.subject: Geography

questions.subject: Geography

questions.subject: Geography
questions.prompt: Two factors that promote rapid chemical weathering in the tropics are
questions.explanation: Chemical weathering is accelerated by warmth and moisture. High temperatures speed up many chemical reactions, while abundant water supports processes such as solution, hydrolysis and oxidation.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. Warm and humid conditions favour rapid chemical weathering.
optionExplanations.B: Low temperatures generally slow chemical reactions.
optionExplanations.C: Extreme aridity limits the water needed for many chemical weathering processes.
optionExplanations.D: Low humidity restricts moisture-dependent chemical reactions.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.prompt: What does subsistence agriculture mean?

questions.prompt: When the gradient of a river channel changes from a steep to a gentle angle, the main activity of the river will be

questions.subject: Geography

questions.subject: Geography

questions.subject: Geography
questions.prompt: Which of the following factors least explains the fast-growing population in Africa?

This is a proportional statement, not necessarily a claim about the absolute number of adults.

optionExplanations.A: High old-age mortality reduces the proportion of people above sixty.
optionExplanations.B: Correct. The two mortality patterns reduce the relative size of the youngest and oldest groups.
optionExplanations.C: The question specifies no migration, so migrant workers are not the explanation.
optionExplanations.D: High infant mortality reduces the proportion of children under five.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: The poorer a country is, the larger the percentage of its labour force generally engaged in
questions.explanation: In lower-income economies, a larger share of workers is commonly employed in agriculture, often with lower labour productivity. As economies develop, employment generally shifts toward manufacturing and services.

optionExplanations.A: Manufacturing employment typically expands as industrialisation progresses.
optionExplanations.B: The civil service is not generally the largest employment sector in poorer economies.
optionExplanations.C: Correct. Agriculture often employs a larger share of the labour force in lower-income countries.
optionExplanations.D: Commerce and trade are important but are not the intended sector in this comparison.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: An indication that there is inflation in a country is that

options.A: The general price level of goods and services falls persistently over time
options.B: The rate of unemployment falls persistently over time
options.C: The general price level of goods and services rises persistently over time
options.D: The value of money increases persistently over time

questions.explanation: Inflation is a sustained increase in the general price level over time. As prices rise, the purchasing power of money generally falls.

optionExplanations.A: A sustained fall in the general price level is deflation.
optionExplanations.B: Falling unemployment is not the definition or necessary indicator of inflation.
optionExplanations.C: Correct. A persistent rise in the general price level is inflation.
optionExplanations.D: Inflation generally reduces, rather than increases, the purchasing power of money.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: The following are reasons for the failure of agricultural policies in West Africa EXCEPT

options.A: Poor implementation and corruption in the execution of agricultural programmes
options.B: Regular provision of subsidized farm inputs and credit facilities to farmers
options.C: A land tenure system that discourages large-scale mechanized farming
options.D: Inadequate rural infrastructure such as roads and storage facilities

questions.explanation: The question asks for the option that is NOT a cause of policy failure. Regular access to subsidised inputs and credit supports farmers and can improve implementation outcomes. Poor implementation, restrictive land tenure and inadequate infrastructure can undermine agricultural programmes.

optionExplanations.A: Poor implementation and corruption can prevent policies from achieving their objectives.
optionExplanations.B: Correct. Regular input and credit support is a facilitating measure, not a cause of policy failure.
optionExplanations.C: Restrictive land tenure can discourage investment and mechanisation.
optionExplanations.D: Poor roads and storage facilities increase costs and post-harvest losses.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: A rise in government expenditure can lead to

options.D: Lower importation of raw materials by industries

questions.explanation: An increase in government expenditure raises aggregate demand. If the economy is near or at capacity, the additional demand can put upward pressure on the general price level and cause demand-pull inflation.

optionExplanations.A: Higher expenditure can increase demand and employment rather than necessarily raise unemployment.
optionExplanations.B: Correct. Higher aggregate demand can create inflationary pressure, especially near full capacity.
optionExplanations.C: Higher demand may raise sales and profits rather than necessarily reduce them.
optionExplanations.D: The effect on imports depends on the composition of spending and supply conditions; it is not the direct intended result.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: A stock exchange is a market that

options.A: Deals with the exchange of commodities
options.B: Deals with the purchase and sale of securities
options.D: Exchanges treasury bills for bills of exchange

questions.explanation: A stock exchange provides an organised market for trading securities such as shares and certain debt instruments. It supports capital formation and liquidity for investors.

optionExplanations.A: Commodity exchanges trade specified commodities, not the securities market described.
optionExplanations.B: Correct. A stock exchange facilitates the buying and selling of securities.
optionExplanations.C: This is not the function of a financial stock exchange.
optionExplanations.D: This confuses different financial instruments and does not define a stock exchange.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: Acceptability, durability, homogeneity and portability are all attributes of good
questions.explanation: Good money should be generally acceptable, durable, uniform or homogeneous, and easy to carry. These characteristics make it useful as a medium of exchange and store of value.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. These are standard characteristics of money.
optionExplanations.B: Markets are not described by these four monetary characteristics.
optionExplanations.C: These are not defining characteristics of government.
optionExplanations.D: Banks are financial institutions, not the item described.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: An agricultural production process which uses more machinery relative to labour is referred to as
questions.explanation: Capital-intensive production uses a relatively high proportion of capital equipment and machinery compared with labour. Large-scale and commercial farming may use machinery, but they describe scale and market orientation rather than the factor-intensity concept.

optionExplanations.A: Land-intensive farming uses a relatively large amount of land per unit of other inputs.
optionExplanations.B: Large-scale farming describes the size of the operation, not necessarily its capital-to-labour ratio.
optionExplanations.C: Correct. Machinery is capital, so a high machinery-to-labour ratio is capital-intensive.
optionExplanations.D: Commercial farming describes production mainly for sale.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: An argument for the use of commercial policy rests on the need to

options.B: Encourage the importation of non-essential goods
options.C: Make a country enjoy absolute advantage in production of all goods

questions.explanation: Commercial policy measures such as tariffs, quotas and targeted support may be used to protect or develop domestic industries and employment. These measures can have costs and trade-offs, but reducing domestic unemployment is a recognised policy objective.

optionExplanations.A: Commercial restrictions can raise import prices rather than make imports more affordable.
optionExplanations.B: Encouraging non-essential imports is not a standard protective-policy objective.
optionExplanations.C: Trade policy cannot guarantee absolute advantage in all goods.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. Protecting or supporting domestic production can be used to support employment.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: An entrepreneur is encouraged to adopt division of labour in production because it

options.A: Leads to increased cost of production and lower output
options.C: Brings about equal cost and employment opportunities
options.D: Leads to increased output and lower cost of production

questions.explanation: Specialisation allows workers to become more skilled at particular tasks, reduces time lost switching between tasks and can support the use of specialised tools. These effects can raise output and reduce unit costs.

optionExplanations.A: This is the opposite of the usual productivity benefit of specialisation.
optionExplanations.B: Employment may be affected in different ways, but this is not the main efficiency reason.
optionExplanations.C: This does not describe the central productivity benefit.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. Division of labour can increase productivity and lower unit production costs.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: Cost-push inflation is caused by a

options.A: Decrease in the cost of production
options.D: Rise in the cost of production

questions.explanation: Cost-push inflation occurs when increases in production costs, such as wages, energy, raw materials or transport, raise firms' unit costs and lead to higher selling prices.

optionExplanations.A: Lower production costs would tend to reduce upward price pressure.
optionExplanations.B: A rise in demand is associated with demand-pull inflation.
optionExplanations.C: Lower transport costs would generally reduce production and distribution costs.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. Rising production costs are the defining cause of cost-push inflation.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: Development plans in West Africa tend to deviate from their targets mainly due to
questions.explanation: Political instability can interrupt policy continuity, change priorities, weaken institutions and delay or reverse planned programmes. These effects make it difficult to meet development-plan targets.

optionExplanations.A: Education levels affect development, but the source identifies political instability as the principal planning obstacle.
optionExplanations.B: Population growth creates pressure on resources but is not the source's intended answer.
optionExplanations.C: Manpower shortages can constrain implementation but are not the intended principal factor here.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. Political instability can disrupt continuity and implementation of development plans.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: Economic problems arise mainly as a result of

options.A: Lack of foresight on the part of resource users
options.B: Inaccurate statistical data in West Africa
options.D: Limitations in the availability of resources

questions.explanation: The fundamental economic problem is scarcity: resources are limited relative to human wants. Scarcity forces individuals and societies to make choices and incur opportunity costs.

optionExplanations.A: Poor foresight may worsen decisions but is not the fundamental source of economic problems.
optionExplanations.B: Inaccurate data can impair planning but does not create the basic economic problem.
optionExplanations.C: Waste can intensify scarcity but is not its underlying definition.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. Limited resources relative to unlimited wants create the basic economic problem.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: Harmonised monetary and fiscal policies are a feature of
questions.explanation: An economic union is a deeper form of regional integration that coordinates or harmonises important economic policies, potentially including monetary and fiscal policies. A free trade area mainly removes internal trade barriers while members retain separate external tariffs.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. An economic union involves deeper policy coordination.
optionExplanations.B: A customs union adds a common external tariff but does not necessarily harmonise monetary and fiscal policy.
optionExplanations.C: A common market allows freer movement of goods and factors but does not by itself require harmonised monetary and fiscal policies.
optionExplanations.D: A free trade area removes internal trade barriers while retaining independent external trade policies.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: If an increase in the price of crude oil leads to an increase in the prices of kerosene and grease, then kerosene and grease are in
questions.explanation: Kerosene and grease are products obtained from refining crude oil. They are jointly supplied because their production is linked to the same raw material and refining process.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. The products are obtained jointly from the refining of crude oil.
optionExplanations.B: Competitive supply describes alternative uses of the same resources where producing more of one reduces the other.
optionExplanations.C: Composite supply is not the standard term for products jointly obtained from one production process.
optionExplanations.D: Market supply refers to the total quantity supplied by all producers.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: If in the short run commodity X and commodity Y are supplied jointly, which of the following is correct?

options.A: An increase in demand for Y will raise the price of X
options.B: An increase in demand for X will cause less of Y to be produced
options.C: An increase in demand for X will increase the supply of Y
options.D: An increase in demand for X will leave the supply of Y unchanged

questions.explanation: When two goods are jointly supplied, they are produced together. An increase in production of X therefore also increases the quantity of Y supplied, assuming the joint production process remains unchanged.

optionExplanations.A: A higher demand for Y may affect its price, but it does not necessarily raise the price of X in the way stated.
optionExplanations.B: Joint production means increasing X does not ordinarily reduce the jointly produced quantity of Y.
optionExplanations.C: Correct. Increasing output of X through joint production also increases the supply of Y.
optionExplanations.D: The supply of Y is linked to the joint production of X, so it does not remain unchanged.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.topic: Variation — direct variation with a squared variable
questions.prompt: A varies directly as b². When A = 4 and b = 1, find A when b = 2.
questions.explanation: If A varies directly as b², then A = kb². Using A = 4 when b = 1 gives 4 = k(1)², so k = 4. When b = 2, A = 4 × 2² = 16.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect. The square of 2 is 4, so the result is 4 × 4 = 16.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect. This does not satisfy A = 4b².
optionExplanations.C: Correct. A = 4 × 2² = 16.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect. This does not satisfy the direct-variation relationship.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.topic: Coordinate geometry — equation of a straight line
questions.prompt: Obtain the equation of a straight line passing through (3, 15) whose slope is 3⅕.
questions.explanation: The slope is 3⅕ = 16/5. Using y − y₁ = m(x − x₁): y − 15 = (16/5)(x − 3). Multiply by 5: 5y − 75 = 16x − 48. Rearranging gives 5y − 16x − 27 = 0.

optionExplanations.A: The x-term has the wrong sign and the constant is incorrect.
optionExplanations.B: The constant term has the wrong sign.
optionExplanations.C: Correct. Rearranging the point-slope equation gives 5y − 16x − 27 = 0.
optionExplanations.D: Both the x-term and constant arrangement are incorrect.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.prompt: Simplify √75 − √12 + √27.
questions.explanation: Simplify each surd: √75 = 5√3, √12 = 2√3 and √27 = 3√3. Therefore 5√3 − 2√3 + 3√3 = 6√3.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect. The coefficients combine to 5 − 2 + 3 = 6.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect. This omits part of the final sum.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect. This omits the positive contribution from √27.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: Monopoly can best be described as a market in which

options.A: A single seller sells a product which has no close substitute
options.B: The entry of other firms is restricted by the few firms in the market
options.C: Two or more sellers sell a differentiated product
options.D: Few sellers sell products at different prices

questions.explanation: A monopoly is a market structure with a single seller supplying a product or service that has no close substitutes, protected by significant barriers to entry.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. A single seller and absence of close substitutes are central characteristics of monopoly.
optionExplanations.B: This describes an oligopolistic market with a small number of firms.
optionExplanations.C: This is more consistent with monopolistic competition.
optionExplanations.D: This describes a market with a few sellers, characteristic of oligopoly.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.prompt: Net migration is the difference between
questions.explanation: Net migration is calculated as the number of immigrants entering a country or region minus the number of emigrants leaving it during a specified period.

optionExplanations.A: This is not a migration measure.
optionExplanations.B: Internal and external migration are categories, not the calculation of net migration.
optionExplanations.C: Population and census are not the components of net migration.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. Net migration equals immigration minus emigration.
